title: Create your workspace
summary: Sign up, name your workspace and choose where your team's data lives.
content:
Your workspace is the home for every project your team plans in Orbitly. It takes about two minutes to set up.

Set up the workspace

  1. Go to the Orbitly sign-up page and enter your work email.
  2. Choose a workspace name. Most teams use the company name.
  3. Pick a data region: United States or European Union. This can't be changed later.
  4. Invite teammates now, or skip and do it later.

What you get

  • A sample project you can explore and delete
  • A 14-day trial of the Team plan, no card needed
  • A personal inbox for mentions and assignments

Tip: Use the same email domain as your colleagues and they can join without an invite.

title: Create your first project
summary: Start from a blank project or a template and add your first tasks.
content:
Projects hold tasks, milestones, files and discussions for one piece of work, like a product launch or an office move.

Start a project

  1. Click New project in the sidebar.
  2. Pick a template, or choose Blank project.
  3. Give it a name, a start date and an optional target date.
  4. Choose who can see it: everyone in the workspace, or invited people only.

Templates worth trying

  • Product launch: phases, a launch milestone and a checklist
  • Client onboarding: a repeatable set of tasks per client
  • Content calendar: weekly columns and a review stage

Tip: You can turn any project into a template later from its settings menu.

title: A quick tour of Orbitly
summary: The sidebar, inbox, project views and search, explained in five minutes.
content:
Orbitly has three main areas. Once you know them, everything else is easy to find.

The sidebar

The sidebar lists your projects, favourites and saved views. Drag projects to reorder them, or star the ones you use daily.

Project views

  • Timeline for dates and dependencies
  • Board for moving work through stages
  • List for fast editing in a table
  • Calendar for deadlines by month

Search

Press / anywhere to search tasks, projects, people and comments.

title: Import projects from spreadsheets or other tools
summary: Bring in tasks from CSV, Trello, Asana or Jira without retyping them.
content:
You can import an existing plan into a new or existing project. Orbitly maps columns for you and shows a preview first.

Import a CSV

  1. Open the project and choose More › Import.
  2. Upload a CSV with one task per row.
  3. Match columns to Orbitly fields such as title, assignee, start and due date.
  4. Review the preview and click Import tasks.

Supported tools

  • Trello boards, including lists and labels
  • Asana projects, including sections and subtasks
  • Jira issues via a CSV export

Tip: Import into a test project first if your spreadsheet is large.

title: Plan work on the timeline
summary: Drag tasks onto dates, resize them to change duration and zoom from days to quarters.
content:
The timeline shows every task with a start and due date as a bar. It is the fastest way to see whether a plan fits.

Schedule tasks

  1. Open a project and switch to Timeline.
  2. Drag a task from the unscheduled list onto the timeline.
  3. Drag either end of a bar to change its dates.
  4. Use the zoom control to switch between days, weeks, months and quarters.

Read the timeline

  • Bars are coloured by assignee or status, your choice
  • A red outline means a task is overdue
  • The vertical line marks today

Tip: Hold Shift while dragging to move a task and everything that depends on it.

title: Set up task dependencies
summary: Link tasks so one can't start until another finishes, and see the critical path.
content:
Dependencies keep a plan honest. When an early task slips, Orbitly shows you which later tasks are affected.

Add a dependency

  1. On the timeline, hover over a task bar until a dot appears at its end.
  2. Drag from the dot to the task that depends on it.
  3. Choose the type: finish-to-start is the most common.

The critical path

Turn on Show critical path to highlight the chain of tasks that decides your end date. Delays on these tasks delay the whole project.

title: Use milestones to mark key dates
summary: Milestones are zero-length markers for launches, reviews and deadlines.
content:
A milestone is a moment, not a task. Use them for dates that matter to people outside the project.

Create a milestone

  1. Click Add on the timeline toolbar and choose Milestone.
  2. Name it and pick a date.
  3. Optionally link tasks that must finish before it.

Share milestones

Milestones appear on the portfolio view and in the weekly digest email, so stakeholders see them without opening the project.

title: Track progress with the portfolio view
summary: See every project's status, owner and next milestone on one page.
content:
The portfolio view is for team leads who look after several projects at once.

What it shows

  • Status: on track, at risk or off track, set by the project owner
  • Percent of tasks complete
  • The next milestone and its date
  • Owner and team

Update a project's status

  1. Open the project and click the status pill next to its name.
  2. Pick a status and add a short note.
  3. The note appears in the portfolio and the weekly digest.

title: Create and assign tasks
summary: Add tasks, set an assignee and due date, and break big work into subtasks.
content:
Tasks are the building blocks of every project. Each one can have an assignee, dates, a description, files and comments.

Add a task

  1. Press N in any project view, or click Add task.
  2. Type a title and press Enter.
  3. Click the task to open details and set an assignee and due date.

Subtasks

Break large tasks into subtasks from the task detail panel. Subtasks have their own assignee and due date, and the parent shows a progress count.

Tip: Type @name and a date like fri in the title to assign and schedule in one go.

title: Work with boards and custom stages
summary: Move tasks across columns and rename stages to match how your team works.
content:
Board view groups tasks into columns by stage. Teams use it for anything with a clear flow, such as design reviews or support requests.

Customise stages

  1. Switch to Board.
  2. Click a column title to rename it, or Add stage to create one.
  3. Drag columns to reorder them.

Work-in-progress limits

Set a limit on a column and it turns amber when the team takes on more than the limit. It's a gentle nudge to finish before starting.

title: Recurring tasks
summary: Repeat a task daily, weekly, monthly or on a custom schedule.
content:
Recurring tasks are created again automatically when you complete them.

Make a task repeat

  1. Open the task and click the due date.
  2. Choose Repeat and pick a schedule.
  3. Decide whether the next copy is based on the due date or the completion date.

title: Use keyboard shortcuts
summary: Move faster with shortcuts for creating, assigning and navigating.
content:
Press ? anywhere in Orbitly to see every shortcut. These are the ones people use most.

Most used

  • N new task
  • / search
  • A assign to me
  • D set due date
  • G then T go to timeline

title: Invite people to your workspace
summary: Send invites by email or share a join link with your company domain.
content:
Anyone with an admin or member role can invite people. Guests can be invited to single projects.

Invite by email

  1. Open Settings › People.
  2. Click Invite and enter one or more email addresses.
  3. Choose a role and click Send invites.

Join by domain

Turn on Allow anyone with an @yourcompany.com email to join and new colleagues can sign up without waiting for an invite.

Tip: Invites expire after 14 days. You can resend them from the People page.

title: Roles and permissions explained
summary: What admins, members and guests can see and do.
content:
Orbitly has three workspace roles. Project owners can also limit who sees a project.

Workspace roles

  • Admin: manages billing, people, security settings and every project
  • Member: creates projects and sees everything shared with the workspace
  • Guest: sees only the projects they are invited to, and can't see the people list

Private projects

Set a project to Invited people only and it disappears from search and the portfolio for everyone else, including members.

title: Remove someone from your workspace
summary: Deactivate an account and reassign their open tasks.
content:
When someone leaves, deactivate their account rather than deleting it, so their history stays intact.

Deactivate a person

  1. Open Settings › People and find the person.
  2. Choose Deactivate.
  3. Pick someone to take over their open tasks, or leave them unassigned.

title: Turn on single sign-on (SSO)
summary: Let people sign in with Okta, Google Workspace or Microsoft Entra ID.
content:
SSO is available on the Business plan. Admins can require it for everyone in the workspace.

Set up SSO

  1. Open Settings › Security and choose Single sign-on.
  2. Pick your identity provider and copy the details shown into it.
  3. Test with your own account before requiring SSO for everyone.

Tip: Keep one admin account that can sign in with a password in case your provider has an outage.

title: Compare plans
summary: Free, Team and Business plans side by side.
content:
Every plan includes unlimited tasks and the timeline. Paid plans add more projects, guests and controls.

At a glance

  • Free: up to 3 projects and 5 people
  • Team: unlimited projects, guests, portfolio view and integrations
  • Business: everything in Team plus SSO, audit log and priority support

Switching plans

Upgrades take effect immediately and you pay the difference for the rest of the billing period. Downgrades take effect at the next renewal.

title: Update payment details and download invoices
summary: Change your card, add a billing email and get past invoices as PDFs.
content:
Only workspace admins can see billing settings.

Download an invoice

  1. Open Settings › Billing.
  2. Scroll to Invoices.
  3. Click the download icon next to the invoice you need.

Billing email

Add a separate billing email, such as your finance team, and invoices are sent there as well.

title: How seats are counted
summary: Who counts as a paid seat, and what happens when you add people mid-cycle.
content:
Members and admins each use a seat. Guests are free on paid plans.

Adding and removing people

  • Adding a member mid-cycle charges a prorated amount on your next invoice
  • Deactivating a member frees the seat right away
  • Credits for unused time are applied at renewal

title: Connect Orbitly to Slack
summary: Get task updates in channels and create tasks from messages.
content:
The Slack integration posts project updates to a channel and lets anyone turn a message into a task.

Connect Slack

  1. Open Settings › Integrations and choose Slack.
  2. Approve the connection in Slack.
  3. In any project, choose Notify a channel and pick the channel.

Create tasks from messages

Hover over a message, open the actions menu and choose Create Orbitly task. The message link is saved on the task.

title: Sync deadlines to your calendar
summary: Subscribe to your tasks in Google Calendar, Outlook or Apple Calendar.
content:
Each person has a private calendar link with their assigned tasks and project milestones.

Subscribe

  1. Open your profile menu and choose Calendar sync.
  2. Copy the private link.
  3. Add it as a subscribed calendar in your calendar app.

Tip: Treat the link like a password. You can reset it at any time.

title: Get started with the Orbitly API
summary: Create an API token and make your first request.
content:
The REST API lets you read and update projects and tasks from your own scripts and tools.

Create a token

  1. Open Settings › API tokens.
  2. Click New token, name it and choose read or read-write access.
  3. Copy the token. It is shown only once.

Limits

  • 120 requests per minute per token
  • Responses are JSON and paginated 100 items at a time
  • Webhooks are available for task and project changes
